jobs.occupation: International Clinician Scientist (f/d/m) for iPRACTIS (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.About usHannover Medical School (MHH) is offering positions in the international clinician scientist program (iPRACTIS), a unique opportunity for internationally mobile researchers with a completed medical degree outside of Germany. Over three years, you will gain experience in translational research while working towards medical degree recognition in Germany.iPRACTIS supports internationally trained researchers aiming to build careers in academic medicine. Over three years, participants will deepen their research experience on a translational research project while working towards integration into the German academic and healthcare system.We offerThe international clinician scientist program iPRACTIS offers:- 36 months of structured clinical and scientific training based on an individually tailored career plan- Individualized support in navigating the process of medical degree recognition in Germany and developing German language proficiency- Funding for materials, travel, and publication- Individualized support from a personalized mentoring team- A curriculum to acquire key competencies [including data management and analysis, GCP clinical investigator certification (GCP-Prüfarztkurs), project management]- Regular evaluations and feedback meetings- A full onboarding program and integration into a strong Clinician Scientist NetworkClinical expectations: Participants will achieve recognition of their medical qualifications along with sufficient German language skills for clinical practice, allowing future specialist training and medical practice in Germany.Research expectations: Participants will develop as a R2 researcher (according to the European Framework for Research Careers), including submitting their first third-party funding application. Participants who complete this process will be ready to pursue an independent research career (R3) in roles such as assistant professor, principal investigator, or junior group leader.Eligibility requirementsTo apply, candidates must:- Hold a completed medical degree (from outside Germany)- Have initial research experience (completed R1 to early R2 based on European Framework for Research Careers)- Have not yet completed specialist clinical training (residency or German 'Facharzt' / 'Weiterbildung' equivalent)- Be committed to pursuing a career combining clinical practice and researchIn order to consider your application, we require that you submit the completed "iPRACTIS Application Template" (download) as well as a cover letter and detailed resume (in table format), a declaration of consent and copies of certificates (medical examination certificates, doctoral degree certificates, high school diplomas, and other relevant certificates and documents. If the documents are not in German or English, a certified translation is requested). Please submit your application as a single PDF file directly to practis@mh-hannover.de. More information can be found at iPRACTIS.External applications for iPRACTIS positions will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline for internal applications is 05.01.2027.For questions, please reach out to Dr. Thorsten Saenger: practis@mh-hannover.de.Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Forschung, Lehrtätigkeit (Hochschule)

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Positions in Attosecond Pulse Generation at EuXFEL (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:Postdoc Positions in Attosecond Pulse Generation at EuXFELRemuneration Group 13 | Limited: 3 years | Starting date: 04.01.2027 | ID: MPO007/2026 | Deadline: 30.11.2026 | Full-time/Part-timeDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.The European XFEL is one of the world's leading free-electron laser facilities and provides intense X-ray pulses with durations down to the attosecond regime. A dedicated strategy program has been established to further develop and exploit these ultrashort pulses, including through recruitment of new expertise. The positions focus on advancing existing techniques for short-pulse generation in terms of power, pulse duration and stability and both the hard and soft x-rays. Key areas of research include:- Independent control of transverse and longitudinal dispersion- Development of advanced pulse-shaping techniques- Advancing the use of existing longitudinal diagnostics for short-pulse characterizationAbout your role:These positions combine scientific R&D with hands-on machine development and operation, providing the opportunity to take new FEL concepts from simulation through experimental validation to routine operation.- Conduct simulations and eventual experiments towards short pulse production at the EuXFEL- Actively support other attosecond generation activities- Communicate results and insights through presentations, reports and publications- Encouraged to develop and pursue their own ideas- Contribute to the reliable daily operation of the facility as an operatorAbout you:- PhD in physics or related field with a background in accelerator or FEL physics- Experience with relevant FEL simulation codes- Good communication skills and a collaborative approach to working in an interdisciplinary team- Good command of English, German is beneficial- Experience in attosecond pulse generation- Practical experience in the FEL field- Experience in cathode shaping, fresh-slice or laser beam modulationGood reasons to join:Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our staff are central to us, with gender equality forming a key part of this commitment. To support work life balance we offer flexible working hours, variable part-time, job-sharing models and participation in mobile work (up to 50%). You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. Remuneration is according to the regulations of the TV-AVH. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations.For further information please contact Marc Guetg (marc.guetg@desy.de (https://mailto:marc.guetg@desy.de) ).Please submit your complete application documents (letter of motivation and research interests, CV, list of publications, relevant certificates and three letters of references). Please use our online tool for the submission of the letters of reference: Additional application documents (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822/2/892)We look forward to receiving your application via our application portal:Apply now! (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822)DESY promotes equal opportunities, diversity and inclusion (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822/2/2544) . We therefore welcome applications from people of all dimensions of diversity. The professional development of women (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822/2/2820) is very important to us and therefore we strongly encourage women to apply for the vacant position. Applications from severely disabled persons and those with equivalent status will be given preference if they are equally qualified (sbv.desy.de (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822/2/780) ).You can find further information here:https://www.desy.de/career/apprenticeship/ (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/134822/2/3781)Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESYHuman Resources Department | Notkestraße 85 | 22607 HamburgPhone: +49 40 8998‑3392 (https://tel:+494089983392)

jobs.description: Job posting no. 20261008The GWDG is seeking aGenerative AI Developer (m/f/d)to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C) with a regular working week of 39 hours (100%). Remuneration is in accordance with the collective agreement for the German public service (federal government); depending on qualifications, the position will be grade TVöD E 13. The position is suitable for part-time work and initially limited till 31rd December 2029. The GWDG strives for long-term cooperation. If interested, there is the possibility of a doctorate.The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG operates the HLRN-IV system “Emmy”, one of the most powerful computers in the world.As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG offers technical support to researchers and students from various science domains using sophisticated computer codes, including earth system science, life science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. At the same time, we aim to improve our close collaboration with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), and specialized computing centers including the German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ) and the Institute for Advanced Simulation Jülich (IAS-JSC).As part of our AI Service Center for Sensitive and Critical Infrastructure (KISSKI) we have created a number of AI-based services that offer high levels of security and privacy due to being processed on our own hardware. The position will be located within the subproject “KISSKI-EvoKS” and closely collaborate with customers from SMEs and Startups to develop prototypes and workflows that lead to PoCs and Blueprints. Those customers will come predominantly from sectors with high data protection requirements.The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, AI, and Machine Learning.ResponsibilitiesWe have a wide range of potential responsibilities that we would like to discuss with you. Your responsibilities in our team could include, for example:- Design appropriate solutions to address customer use cases building upon our existing AI infrastructure- Support for companies in the development of AI services- Generating blueprints and whitepapers- Document solutions for internal knowledge sharing and customer handover- Representation at workshops and conferences- Integration of novel AI solutions into our AI service portfolio- Integration of novel AI solutions into the SAIA Platform (Scalable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Accelerator)Requirements- Successfully completed master's degree in computer science or related fields- Very good programming skills in a high-level programming language, primarily Python- Very good Linux skills (e.g. Bash scripting, Git, containers)- Good knowledge of software engineering (security, testing)- Good knowledge of DevOps (e.g. Gitlab, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, pytest)- Good knowledge of databases (SQLModel, SQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite)- Experience with web development (HTTP, FastAPI, HTML, JavaScript)- Basics in generative AI (e.g. LLMs, diffusion models, and use with Pytorch or Tensorflow)- Excellent analytical skills- Excellent problem-solving skills- Very good German skills (C1)- Very good English skills (C1)- Willingness to travel on businessDesirable- Ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical customers- Experience with customer-facing technical roles- Basics in agile software development (e.g. Kanban, Scrum)- Experience with service-oriented user support- Exposure to HPC, scientific computing, or data-intensive domains- Experience with the use of HPC systems (e.g. SLURM)Our offer- Flexible working hours and opportunity for mobile working- A modern, diverse, and exceptional work environment with close proximity to academia and research at the intersection of several innovative technology sectors- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center- Collaboration in a competent and committed team- Qualification and further development of your skills- Social benefits of the public sectorYour applicationHave we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 08.11.2026 via our online form: https://bewerbermanagement.net/r32hzThe GWDG strives for gender equity and diversity and therefore welcomes applications from any background. The GWDG strives to employ more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged.If you have any questions about the advertised position, please contact Prof. Dr. Julian Kunkel (e-mail: julian.kunkel@gwdg.de).Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung
